pr_title: *: fix revoke statement for CURRENT_USER() and refine error message
pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #23850   (Need to verify: The expected result is wrong?)

```
mysql> SHOW GRANTS;
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
| Grants for User                                           |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
| GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON *.* TO 'u4'@'%' WITH GRANT OPTION |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

mysql> REVOKE ALL ON *.* FROM CURRENT_USER();
ERROR 1105 (HY000): Unknown user: @
```

Problem Summary:

The user name and host part for REVOKE ... FROM CURRENT_USER is missing.

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:

Fill the user name and host part for CURRENT_USER.

How it Works:

Fix bug.

### Related changes

- Need to cherry-pick to the release branch

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Unit test


### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->

- Fix 'REVOKE ... FROM CURRENT_USER()' statement. The host and username is not set for CURRENT_USER and that cause the statement fail.
pr_comments: /LGTM

> Issue Number: close #23850 (Need to verify: The expected result is wrong?)

I commented in the issue, but I got this out of the MTR tests for 8.0. I think it's fine to stay with 5.7 for now and fix it when we move to MySQL 8.0 compatibility. The current behavior is not neccessarily wrong.

I have another PR which fixes some other revoke bugs: https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/23946 - the error messages are not technically MySQL compatible. I think we can create an issue after these merge and leave it for new contributors.

issue_context.title: REVOKE ALL fails on current user
comments:
I find it's caused by the 'Grant Option'  privilege.

According to the MySQL document https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/revoke.html, the privilege check rule for 'revoke some privilege':

> To use the first REVOKE syntax, you must have the GRANT OPTION privilege, and you must have the privileges that you are revoking.

However, the rule for 'revoke some privilege' and 'revoke all privilege' are different. 'revoke all privileges' check 'CREATE USER' and so on.

> To use this REVOKE syntax, you must have the global CREATE USER privilege, or the UPDATE privilege for the mysql system schema.

That is the root cause.
